players.product: Electron small launch and Neutron medium-lift launch vehicle (in development)

quarterly_data.signal: Rocket Lab Q2 2026 results: record revenue of $234 million, up 62% year-over-year and 16.8% sequentially; Space Systems $189.5 million (up 38.6% sequentially, driven by satellite manufacturing and initial Mynaric contribution); Launch Services $44.6 million (down 30% from Q1 on a similar number of launches, due to the mix of point-in-time Electron and over-time HASTE revenue).

Rocket Lab margins: Q2 GAAP gross margin 36.1% (above 33%-35% guidance) and non-GAAP 41.5% (above 38%-40%), with a non-recurring tariff refund benefit largely offset by an inventory reserve against the Neutron Flight 2 launch vehicle; adjusted EBITDA loss $8.8 million.

Rocket Lab Q3 2026 guidance: CFO, turning to 'our guidance for the third quarter of 2026': 'We expect revenue in the second quarter to range between $250 million and $265 million, representing 10% quarter-over-quarter revenue growth at the midpoint' (the transcript reads 'second quarter' inside the third-quarter guidance); GAAP gross margin 29%-31% and non-GAAP gross margin 35%-37%, accounting for a shift in mix within Space Systems, with a beneficial remixing impact expected beyond Q3; third quarter non-GAAP operating expenses $121 million to $127 million and adjusted EBITDA loss $17 million to $23 million.
quarterly_data.figure: $250 million and $265 million; 29%-31%; 35%-37%; $17 million and $23 million

quarterly_data.signal: Rocket Lab backlog: approximately $2.36 billion at the end of Q2 (launch approximately 40%, Space Systems 60%), with approximately 45.5% expected to convert to revenue within 12 months; more than $1 billion of new contracts signed across Q2 and the period after - more than $437 million of launch bookings (Electron, HASTE, Neutron) and more than $581 million in Space Systems.

Rocket Lab HASTE contract: a record $266 million contract from the U.S. Space Force for up to 18 suborbital missile defense launches, Rocket Lab's largest launch contract ever and its second multi-year DoD suborbital deal in five months; launches mostly from two new pads at Kodiak, Alaska deployed with the GHOST containerized launch-site technology; CFO: the contract includes funding for infrastructure.

Rocket Lab Flatellite contract: a $397 million contract to build and launch multiple Flatellite spacecraft for the Space Force Space-Based Airborne Moving Target Indicator program, to be launched on Neutron; CEO: it is the first Flatellite order, and most of what he could see Rocket Lab doing for itself in the future will be built on the back of a Flatellite platform.

Rocket Lab GEO satellites: two deals totaling more than $160 million to build three geostationary satellites, including a prime contract with the Space Systems Command for two GEO space-domain-awareness satellites carrying the Heimdall payload from acquired GEOST - Rocket Lab's first step into the government GEO satellite market.

Rocket Lab launch bookings: 26 new launches grew the launch backlog to 90+ launches, the highest in its history; 13 launches this year with 100% mission success; NASA signed three Electron launches across two missions next year; iQPS signed another three launches (18 in total); a confidential defense prime booked two HASTE launches in 2027.

Rocket Lab VICTUS HAZE: for the Space Force mission Rocket Lab launched Electron in 16 hours and 42 minutes against a 24-hour requirement, commissioned the spacecraft it built in 38 hours (72 allowed) and tracked, chased and photographed a non-cooperative satellite in less than 59 hours (84 allowed); CEO: the first time the Space Force had ever seen a single prime contractor deliver the rocket, the spacecraft and the orbit operations for the same tactically responsive space mission.

Rocket Lab Iridium acquisition (pending): Iridium brings a constellation of 66 satellites relied upon by more than 2.5 million subscribers and more than $870 million in annual revenue; completion expected in mid-2027 subject to Iridium stockholder and regulatory approvals; CEO: the constellation is good into 2035, growth focus on IoT, direct to device, advanced PNT, defense and aviation / marine safety. Mynaric and Motiv acquisitions closed in the quarter; CEO: likely further tuck-ins, Iridium not a one and done.

Rocket Lab Neutron: production lines up with target delivery of Neutron to the pad in Q4 2026, though the window for an end-of-year launch is narrowing; more than 400 Archimedes hot fires completed and the full engine set for the first launch is in production; stage testing is the last big milestone before flight; planned ramp of 1-3-5 launches.

Rocket Lab Neutron pricing and demand: CFO: Neutron was brought to market at a $50 million-$55 million ASP with no significant discounting for early launches, and sees more upside to ASPs than downside; CEO: zero issues selling full-price Neutrons before the test flight; very limited Neutron supply is being allocated between commercial customers, the government (NSSL) and Rocket Lab's own needs including Iridium.

Rocket Lab launch market: CEO: launch has never been so constrained and options to book a launch, especially after 2029, are extremely limited; the NSSL Lane 1 ceiling tripled from $5.6 billion-$17 billion; competitors' new capacity is largely spoken for by their own internal programs (internets, AI data centers), so the constrained launch market should persist for quite some time.

Rocket Lab space components: CEO: Rocket Lab has scaled its solar business into the largest space-grade solar manufacturer in the world; spacecraft components such as reaction wheels are a moat. CFO: component margins range from the 30s for solar to north of 70 points for some products; satellite platform programs such as SDA Tranche 2 and Tranche 3 (the biggest pieces of backlog) are in the mid-30s; government programs last about four years on a 10/40/40/10 revenue curve.

Rocket Lab orbital data centers: CEO: data centers in space are a real opportunity but he is cautious on their scale; Rocket Lab has released new solar cells specifically targeted at that application and expects to be well positioned if they become real, but is not going to build orbital data centers itself yet.

Rocket Lab Germany: CEO: following the Mynaric acquisition Rocket Lab plans the official establishment of Rocket Lab Germany, seeing a real opportunity to establish a regional hub for constellation-class manufacturing and full-scale spacecraft assembly, integration and test, serving European commercial, civil and defense programs as a domestic provider; Germany has put over $40 billion in place for a satellite missile warning system among other things.

Rocket Lab operating costs and cash: Q2 GAAP operating expenses $142.1 million and non-GAAP $115.7 million; total headcount 3,217 (up 439); capex $26 million; operating cash use $84.1 million and non-GAAP free cash flow use $110.1 million. CFO: the first successful Neutron test launch is the turning point to adjusted EBITDA positivity in the quarter after it, and cash flow positivity will probably come 18-24 months after that pivot; Q3 negative free cash flow expected to remain at elevated levels.
Rocket Lab Mars Telecommunications Orbiter: CEO: Rocket Lab is waiting for NASA to complete its procurement process and feels strongly positioned.

connects_to.relationship: dedicated launch of Kepler's next set of satellites (on-orbit compute, optical comms, hosted payloads) to low Earth orbit

contracts.signal: CEO, on new Neutron contracts: 'today we announced a dedicated launch for Kepler Communications to deliver their next set of satellites to low Earth orbit', expanding Kepler's network capacity with on-orbit compute, optical comms and hosted payloads; the first time Kepler has booked an entire rocket for its constellation rather than rideshare - another strong signal, he said, of the expectation for Neutron to become the industry's alternate ride to space for medium-lift missions.

quarterly_data.signal: Rocket Lab Mynaric: the Mynaric acquisition closed within Q2 and made an initial contribution to Space Systems revenue at lower gross margins; CFO: the asset had supply chain issues and went through an insolvency process, Rocket Lab had to replenish its supply chain (part of the Q2 cash step-up), volumes rise over the next several quarters, and margins should come in line with the rest of the Space Systems merchant business within a few quarters.
